profile_text.body:
Credo AI is a company founded in 2020 that sells an AI governance platform, according to its website. The company describes itself as having created the AI governance category and says its platform is built to help enterprises discover AI systems, enforce policy, manage AI risk, and prove compliance across models, agents, applications, and vendors. It says the platform is built on a Knowledge Graph that combines regulatory intelligence with a customer's business context, and that it draws on more than 300 integrations. Credo AI also says it offers GAIA (Govern AI Assistant) inside the platform, and pre-built policy packs covering the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, and other standards. The company says its policy packs are written by staff who have worked with ISO, NIST, the EU Parliament, NATO, and OECD.

The site presents agent governance as a current focus, describing a registry for agents and agent-specific risk and controls, with agents treated as governed entities that are registered, risk-assessed, sanctioned, and governed. Credo AI positions the product as purpose-built for governance rather than as AI features added to an existing GRC tool. The site quotes customers and partners including Mastercard and IBM, and says enterprises in insurance, financial services, federal, and healthcare use the platform.

The site's own framing is promotional, calling Credo AI the trusted leader in AI governance and describing Measurable Trust as an outcome of the platform. No litigation, SEC filings, patent records, or MCP server listings are recorded for the company.
